question: What are the distances from the point \(P(-3,4)\) to the x-axis and the y-axis, respectively? (Separate your answers with a comma.)
solution: The distance to the x-axis is the absolute value of the y-coordinate, \(|4|=4\). The distance to the y-axis is the absolute value of the x-coordinate, \(|-3|=3\).

edges.reason: The stated rule for a negative input returns its opposite; solving |x|=a also identifies the opposite pair.
Point-to-point shortest-distance language is a helpful model, but perpendicular-shortest distance is a separate fact and not derived merely from the two-point line axiom.
The distance in question is the length of the perpendicular from the point, so perpendicularity identifies which segment is measured.

Absolute difference is one valid length formula. Sorting the coordinates and subtracting the smaller from the larger, or counting grid units, meets the actual criterion without evaluating absolute-value expressions.
